t: Jehovah's Witnesses believe that Jehovah is the only true god and not part of a Trinity, that Jesus is God's first creation, and that Armageddon is imminent and will be followed by an earthly paradise.

The movement grew from Charles Taze Russell's Bible Students, and under Joseph Rutherford adopted the name Jehovah's witnesses in 1931, introduced door-to-door preaching and moved to a centrally directed organisation.

Witnesses refuse military service, saluting flags and blood transfusions of whole blood; they were persecuted in Nazi Germany, where about 2,000 were sent to concentration camps, and are banned or restricted in some countries today.
dyk: In 1912 Charles Taze Russell was the most distributed Christian author in the United States, and in 2010 The Watchtower and Awake! were the world's most widely distributed magazines.
ev: Charles Taze Russell and others form a Bible study group in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania
Zion's Watch Tower Tract Society is co-founded to organise and print the movement's publications
Joseph Franklin Rutherford is elected president of the Society in a disputed election, and tens of thousands leave in the following years
At a convention in Columbus, Ohio, Rutherford introduces the name Jehovah's witnesses
About 20,000 Witnesses live in Nazi Germany, and about 10,000 of them are imprisoned over the following years
The full New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures is released
After publications built expectation that Christ's thousand-year reign might begin, a failed prediction is followed by a decline in membership
Authority for doctrinal and organisational decisions passes from the Society's president to the Governing Body

f.origin: The United States: a Bible study group formed by Charles Taze Russell and others in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in 1870, which became the Bible Student movement; the name Jehovah's witnesses was adopted in 1931.
f.founder: Charles Taze Russell, who co-founded Zion's Watch Tower Tract Society in 1881; Joseph Franklin Rutherford, who kept control of the Society after Russell's death and adopted the name in 1931.
f.scriptures: The Protestant canon of the Bible, held to be inspired and inerrant, read in their own New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures (full version 1961); doctrine is stated through Watch Tower Society publications such as The Watchtower and Awake!
f.followers: About 9.2 million members worldwide reported in 2025, with about 9 million publishers in about 119,500 congregations; independent demographic studies suggest only about half of those who identify as Witnesses are counted as active by the faith itself.
